    Power calculations for co-primary diagnostic accuracy endpoints - Single-test design

    power.copr.test.Rd

    Computes either the required total sample size or the achieved overall power of a single-test confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study with co-primary endpoints (sensitivity and specificity). Exactly one of N and power must be NULL. The one that is NULL is calculated.

    Both endpoints are tested for superiority against fixed null values. Study success requires rejection of both null hypotheses. Overall power is therefore defined under an intersection-union testing (IUT) framework. Under this framework the global type I error rate is controlled at level \(\alpha\) without multiplicity adjustment.

    The calculation explicitly accounts for the assumed disease prevalence, which determines the expected number of diseased and non-diseased subjects.

    power.copr.test(
  N = NULL,
  power = NULL,
  prev,
  se.e,
  se.min,
  sp.e,
  sp.min,
  alpha = 0.025,
  ci_method = c("wald", "logit"),
  alternative = c("one.sided", "two.sided"),
  exact = FALSE,
  exact_rule = c("first", "stays_above")
)

    Arguments

    N

    Total sample size, or NULL to calculate it.

    power

    Desired overall power, or NULL to calculate it.

    prev

    Disease prevalence (0 < prev < 1).

    se.e

    Sensitivity under the alternative hypothesis.

    se.min

    Sensitivity under the null hypothesis.

    sp.e

    Specificity under the alternative hypothesis.

    sp.min

    Specificity under the null hypothesis.

    alpha

    Type I error level (default 0.025).

    ci_method

    Normal approximation method: "wald" (default) or "logit".

    alternative

    "one.sided" (default) or "two.sided".

    exact

    Experimental. Use the exact binomial power instead of the normal approximation, see Details. Default FALSE.

    exact_rule

    Only for exact = TRUE and a given power: "first" (default) or "stays_above".

    Value

    An object of class "power.htest", a list with the elements:

    n

    Total sample size.

    n_dis

    Total number of diseased subjects.

    n_nondis

    Total number of non-diseased subjects.

    prev

    Disease prevalence.

    sig.level

    Type I error level.

    alternative

    "one.sided" or "two.sided".

    power

    Overall power.

    power_se

    Power for the sensitivity endpoint.

    power_sp

    Power for the specificity endpoint.

    ci_method

    Normal approximation used.

    exact

    Whether exact binomial power was used.

    target_power

    Requested power (only when power was given).

    exact_rule

    Rule used (only for exact = TRUE and a given power).

    Details

    Let \(\pi\) denote the assumed disease prevalence. The study population is partitioned into diseased (\(N_{\mathrm{Se}} = N\pi\)) and non-diseased (\(N_{\mathrm{Sp}} = N(1-\pi)\)) independent subgroups.

    Endpoint-specific powers are based on large-sample normal approximations for binomial proportions, using either:

    • the Wald approximation on the probability scale, or

    • the logit-transformed normal approximation.

    Overall power is the probability that both tests reject. Because the endpoints are independent, this equals $$\mathrm{Power}_{\mathrm{Overall}} = \mathrm{Power}_{\mathrm{Se}} \times \mathrm{Power}_{\mathrm{Sp}}.$$

    When prevalence is very low or very high, one subgroup may require substantially more subjects than the other. A naive calculation (taking the maximum of two independently calculated sample sizes) may therefore overpower one endpoint. When power is given, the required total sample size is instead the smallest integer \(N\) for which the overall power reaches the target. It is found by bracketing (doubling) and bisection.

    Exact power (experimental). With exact = TRUE the power is the exact binomial probability that both tests reject. This option is still experimental: it needs further development and testing, and its interface and results may change. It is not monotone in \(N\) (it is a sawtooth), so the bisection is replaced by a vectorised scan over integer \(N\) in a window around the asymptotic solution (0.5 to 1.5 times, extended automatically if needed). Subgroup sizes are round(N * prev) and the remainder, and N must be an integer. exact_rule selects the sample size:

    • "first": the smallest \(N\) reaching the target power. The power may fall below the target again for slightly larger \(N\).

    • "stays_above": the smallest \(N\) from which the power stays at or above the target for all larger \(N\).

    The methodology follows the joint sample size framework for single-arm confirmatory diagnostic accuracy studies of Stark and Zapf (2020).

    References

    Stark, M., & Zapf, A. (2020). Sample size calculation and re-estimation based on the prevalence in a single-arm confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 29(10), 2958–2971. doi:10.1177/0962280220913588

    Author

    Ainesh Sewak & Maia Muresan (DCR Bern)

    Examples

    # Sample size for 80% power
power.copr.test(power = 0.80, prev = 0.5,
                se.e = 0.85, se.min = 0.65,
                sp.e = 0.85, sp.min = 0.55)
#> 
#>      Single-test design (sample size calculation)
#>               Wald normal approximation 
#> 
#>               n = 78
#>           n_dis = 39
#>        n_nondis = 39
#>            prev = 0.5
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.8057111
#>        power_se = 0.8105199
#>        power_sp = 0.994067
#>       ci_method = wald
#>           exact = FALSE
#>    target_power = 0.8
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#> 

# Power for a fixed sample size
power.copr.test(N = 122, prev = 0.5,
                se.e = 0.85, se.min = 0.65,
                sp.e = 0.85, sp.min = 0.55,
                ci_method = "logit")
#> 
#>      Single-test design (power calculation)
#>            Logit normal approximation 
#> 
#>               n = 122
#>           n_dis = 61
#>        n_nondis = 61
#>            prev = 0.5
#>       sig.level = 0.025
#>     alternative = one.sided
#>           power = 0.9479505
#>        power_se = 0.9498933
#>        power_sp = 0.9979548
#>       ci_method = logit
#>           exact = FALSE
#> 
#> NOTE: n is the total sample size.
#>
